Mastermind is a native TanStack Start + Void + Vite+ Cloudflare Worker in
`apps/mastermind`, served only on `mastermind.tuturuuu.com`. The Worker
rejects `tuturuuu.com/mastermind` and its children, which the gateway
redirects to the dedicated host ([no apex path hosting](#no-apex-path-hosting)).
It does not revive the retired app.

## Command center

`/en` and `/vi` render the owner command center with the shared `Structure`
shell and `@tuturuuu/ui` components. Every section reads the
[fleet sync](/platform/features/mobile-mastermind#fleet-sync) snapshot, and
nothing renders a value the snapshot does not carry:

- **What's happening now**: one sentence and four counts (running lanes,
  open asks that need the owner, sign-ins waiting, machines online).
- **Inbox**: open asks in urgent, needs-a-decision and FYI tiers, ordered by
  deadline. A card shows Why, If no answer, From and a live countdown. The
  recommended option answers in one tap; other options, Hold and Reply sit
  beside it. A tapped answer waits five seconds with **Undo** before it is
  sent, then shows the receipt (waiting for pickup or picked up, with the
  revision). Answers use one idempotency key per answer, reused on retry.
  The Answered tab lists recorded answers and decisions resolved elsewhere
  (WhatsApp, the phone, the CLI) in the last 24 hours.
- **Snooze** is per device: Web keeps no per-owner snooze record, so a snooze
  lives in this browser's storage, hides the ask until the chosen time and
  never changes its deadline or what the phone shows.
- **Access requests**: login decisions with the allowlisted link, the device
  code with Copy, the expiry countdown, the waiting, approved and verified
  steps, and "I signed in" (the `signed_in` answer). A request whose expiry
  passes on the page clock reads as expired and hides its link and code.
- **Fleet**: the main freeze, production, migrations and incidents strip
  from `release`, then machines with their lanes. Provider quota is not in
  the snapshot, so its card says so.
- **Activity** is built from the snapshot's own timestamps (asks, resolved
  decisions, failed or waiting lanes, incidents, the production deploy).
- **Approvals** tabulates recorded answers and recent resolutions.
- **Cost and health** links to `/admin`; no spend or error budget reaches
  Mastermind. **Notifications** describes the decision push and keeps the
  per-device "Show FYI" switch.

Page state is one union (ready, stale, unpublished, error). A snapshot older
than ten minutes, an offline orchestrator or a failed refresh keeps the last
snapshot on screen marked stale. The page refreshes every 15 seconds through
TanStack Query; route changes between locales show a fixed skeleton.

## Request admission

Every path, including assets and server functions, passes the Worker first.
Missing configuration fails closed with 503 before storage, API or hub reads.
Signing keys come from the team Access certs endpoint over HTTPS. A JWKS fetch
error denies the request with 403 before any application data reads.

1. Require HTTPS and exactly `mastermind.tuturuuu.com`.
   Preview and workers.dev hosts are refused regardless of forwarded headers.
2. Verify `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` using RS256, issuer
   `https://<CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN>`, `CF_ACCESS_AUD`, expiry and issue time.
   jose's `createRemoteJWKSet` fetches
   `https://<CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN>/cdn-cgi/access/certs`. Its per-team,
   per-isolate cache uses a five-minute refetch cooldown, a ten-minute maximum
   cache age and a five-second fetch timeout. Unknown signing keys fail closed
   during cooldown; a rotated key can be accepted after a successful refetch.
   No static signing-key configuration or network-error fallback is used.
3. Bind the session to the Access identity. Verify the satellite access
   session with `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, target `mastermind`,
   access scope and a maximum lifetime of 300 seconds, and require its email
   to equal the JWT email. The request-injected `getSatelliteAppSessionUser`
   adapter uses shared auth core without the legacy helper's database fallback.
4. When the JWT email equals `MASTERMIND_OWNER_EMAIL`, require `OWNER_IDS`
   membership on every request. Missing or empty IDs deny access. Session
   permission scopes are never treated as permission evidence.
5. For that owner, require live root access on every request:
   `GET /api/v1/mastermind/access` with the owner's session must answer
   `enabled: true` (five-second timeout, redirects refused). The owner never
   falls back to a Fleet grant. Its staging verification with real permission
   removal remains a cutover gate.
6. Any other verified email is a [Fleet grantee](#fleet-access-admission) and
   reaches Fleet paths only.

### Fleet access admission

A person with a live Fleet grant opens only the
[Fleet area](/platform/features/fleet-access#mastermind-web). Every other path
answers 403 before any session refresh, permission check or render, with no
login redirect. Fleet paths are:

- `GET /{en,vi}/fleet-access`;
- `GET /assets/*`;
- `/_serverFn/fleet-access.<name>` for the functions in
  `src/fleet-access/api.ts`, under the same-origin POST rule below.

Production builds give server functions a SHA-256 ID. The Vite config's
`generateFunctionId` pins readable IDs only for the exports listed in
`src/native/fleet-admission.ts`, and the Worker matches them exactly. The
command center's functions keep hashed IDs and stay owner-only. A test fails
when `api.ts` exports a function the list does not name.

Each Fleet request rechecks `GET /api/v1/fleet/access` with the grantee's
session and requires `enabled: true` and `stopped: false`. There is no memo:
a revoked or stopped grant denies the next request, and a failed or
redirected check denies. The request context sets a Fleet actor for every
role but the owner identity only for the owner, so `currentOwner()` throws for
a grantee. The Fleet API checks the live grant again on every read and write.

**Required Access policy change (not applied).** The Access application
admits only the owner. Grantees need an additional Allow rule on the same
application: Google IdP, an explicit email list or Access group kept in step
with the live Fleet grants, the same 24-hour session cap and audit logs. Do
not widen the existing owner rule or add a path-scoped bypass; the Worker
enforces the path boundary. Removing someone from the rule ends their Access
session; revoking the grant denies the next request on its own. Applying the
rule needs release-authority approval.

The Access policy must cover all paths, use Google IdP, allow only the
approved owner and the listed Fleet grantees, cap sessions at 24 hours and
enable audit logs.

## Session issuance

`mastermind` is a registered internal app on `https://mastermind.tuturuuu.com`
only (`PRODUCTION_INTERNAL_APP_DOMAINS`), so the central login hands off to it
like every other satellite. No other host, subdomain or path maps to it.

1. A navigation that passes Access but carries no valid session goes to
   `/login`, which answers 303 to `https://tuturuuu.com/login` with
   `returnUrl=https://mastermind.tuturuuu.com/verify-token?nextUrl=<path>`.
   Return paths must stay on the host and never point at `/login` or
   `/verify-token`.
2. Web mints a single-use, 300-second cross-app token for target
   `mastermind` after its own MFA policy. `/verify-token` exchanges it at
   `POST /api/v1/auth/cross-app-token/verify` and accepts the answer only when
   the access and refresh tokens verify locally for target `mastermind`, the
   token email equals the Access email and the access session lives at most
   300 seconds. For the owner's email the subject must be in `OWNER_IDS`; for
   any other email the new session must hold a live Fleet grant.
3. Both credentials are set host-only (no `Domain`), `Path=/`, `HttpOnly`,
   `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, and the owner returns to the path.
4. When the access session expires, the next request sends the refresh
   credential to `POST /api/v1/auth/cross-app-session/refresh` (after verifying
   it locally for an allowlisted owner, or for the Access email of a grantee),
   renders with the new session and sets
   the rotated cookies on that response. Web's replay grace covers concurrent
   requests. A non-navigation without a session is 403.

`FIXED_INTERNAL_APP_SESSION_CAPS` in `@tuturuuu/auth/app-session-policy` caps
Mastermind at a 300-second access session, a 60-second refresh-early window
and a one-day refresh credential. The resolver and `createAppSessionTokenPair`
both apply it, so no `APP_COORDINATION_SESSION_POLICY` value can loosen it.
`mastermind` is not in `ALL_SATELLITE_APP_SESSION_TARGETS`: its session opens
only the routes that name it (`/api/v1/mastermind/access`, fleet state and
answers). `OWNER_ONLY_INTERNAL_APPS` (`@tuturuuu/utils/owner-only-apps`) keeps
it out of the credentialed accounts CORS origins and API cost identity. The
database audience `private.cross_app_internal_app_names()` lists it
(migration `20261121123000_mastermind_cross_app_token_audience`).

**Worker-only redemption.** Web's verify and refresh routes redeem a
`mastermind` handoff token or refresh credential only with the
`x-tuturuuu-app-redeem-proof` header: an HMAC-SHA256 of the target and the
credential under the coordination secret (`@tuturuuu/auth/app-redeem-proof`;
any current or next secret verifies). Only the Worker and Web hold that
secret, so a handoff URL copied from history or logs, or a refresh cookie
lifted from the browser, mints nothing elsewhere. The Worker also rejects a
refresh credential that lives longer than a day.

**Revocation.** Removing the owner from the Worker's `OWNER_IDS` or from
Web's root Mastermind permission denies the next request and every refresh.
Ending the Access session stops the Worker, the only party that can redeem
the refresh credential. An access session already issued stays valid at the
Web fleet routes until it expires, at most 300 seconds.

## Data boundaries and memo

Data moves only through two server functions, `loadFleet` (GET) and
`answerFleetDecision` (POST), which run after every admission gate and read
the owner from the request context. `createFleetClient` calls
`GET /api/v1/mastermind/fleet/state` (with
`x-mastermind-fleet-features: login`) and
`POST /api/v1/mastermind/fleet/decisions/{id}/answer` with only the owner's
satellite bearer, refuses redirects, applies an eight-second timeout and
validates every body against the shared contract in
`apps/web/src/lib/mastermind/fleet`. Those Web routes admit the Mastermind
satellite session (target `mastermind`, scope `internal-app:session`) next
to the Web session; the owner allowlist and root permission still apply.
The browser never calls an app API directly. The uncalled ops-hub and org
scaffolds keep their constraints: replace the hub stub with the gateway HMAC
assertion path and pass C1 API acceptance before use. There is no second
person store.

The memo factory is per-isolate, keyed by owner ID, bounded to 32 entries and
expires after 60 seconds or session expiry. Run authentication and the owner
gate before consulting it. Removing an owner from the request environment
revokes immediately. A future live permission memo must preserve the same
maximum revocation window and test real permission removal with C1.
All responses are `private, no-store`; no people data may use edge caches.

## Security and verification

After admission, GET and HEAD pass; POST passes only under the app's
`_serverFn/` base with `Origin` equal to the request origin and
`Sec-Fetch-Site` absent or `same-origin`. Every other method or path is 405.
Start's CSRF middleware checks server functions again.

The Worker creates a 128-bit nonce per response. The router (`ssr.nonce`),
the base head script and the theme script stamp it on every script, and the
policy is `script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'` with `style-src 'self'`,
`object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`, `form-action 'self'` and
`frame-ancestors 'none'`; there is no `unsafe-inline`. Responses without a
document run no scripts. Server-rendered `style` attributes are refused, so
`Structure`'s width variables come from `.mastermind-shell` in the app
stylesheet, and menus are non-modal so no scroll-lock stylesheet is injected.
HSTS, nosniff, DENY and no-referrer apply to denied responses too.

On an admitted host run
`ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd apps/mastermind test`.
The matrix signs real JWTs and app sessions and asserts 403 with zero reads.
It also checks JWKS fetch failure, unknown keys, rotation after cooldown,
apex-path refusal and the POST method gate. It covers immediate owner revocation, memo expiry and isolation, user-credential
forwarding and a recursive privileged-key-name scan.
The owning native workflow builds in CI, then seals and restores the Worker.
Its explicit test:runtime command runs the .acceptance.mjs suite against the
emitted artifact; generic source-test discovery must not run that suite. The
suite serves a synthetic fleet snapshot, renders both locales and requires
every `<script>` to carry the response's CSP nonce, a fresh nonce per
response, and 405 for a cross-site server-function POST. Runtime
fixtures use isolated .invalid preview hosts. The source auth matrix also checks
the production-like preview hostname.
The local emitted-Worker fixture sets `dev.origin.secure: true` while its
listener remains on loopback HTTP. The runner otherwise rewrites HTTPS inputs to
HTTP before the Worker sees them, and the required HTTPS guard correctly denies
the owner before JWT verification. Preserve the hostname without an origin-host
override so preview and apex hosts still fail. The source matrix separately
asserts that a plaintext HTTP owner request returns 403 with zero reads.

## No apex path hosting

Mastermind is served only on `mastermind.tuturuuu.com`. With
`GATEWAY_MASTERMIND_REDIRECT=1`, which the release owner sets on the gateway
once the host passes acceptance, the gateway answers `tuturuuu.com/mastermind`
and its children with a plain 302 to it (path suffix and query kept, no
proxying, also in passthrough mode). The build is pinned to the root
(`basePath: ''`). Mounting it on the shared `tuturuuu.com` origin was
reviewed and rejected, because nothing can bind the caller there:

- Every Web page is same-origin with the mount. A Web script can set
  `referrer` to a `/mastermind` URL, `history.pushState` there, or
  `window.open('/mastermind/…')` and script the opened document, so
  `Sec-Fetch-Site`, a `Referer` path, a CSRF token read from the page and a
  double-submit cookie all pass. GET server functions (`loadFleet`) would
  also return the snapshot, login links and device codes to that script.
- A session derived from the shared root session makes every same-origin
  request carrying it the owner. Cookie isolation (`isolation` in the mount
  config, which the Worker never applies today) would still forward an
  access-token-only Supabase session.
- An Access path application only proves Access passed the request: a Web
  page's fetch of `/mastermind/*` carries `CF_Authorization` and receives a
  real assertion. Its defaults are domain-scoped, readable by script and
  `SameSite=None`.
- `localStorage` is per origin, and Web's service worker (scope `/`) would
  intercept the mount.

Any future proposal must survive a real-browser matrix with the owner signed
in: Web-page GET and POST to both server functions (also after `pushState`,
with a forged `referrer` and from a `window.open` opener) return 403 with no
snapshot data and zero upstream calls; framing is refused; the service
worker never answers the mount; `CF_Authorization` is `Path=/mastermind`,
`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` and absent from `/` and `/api/`; AUDs
are per host; the app-visible cookies hold no Web, app or Supabase session;
and owner removal is immediate.

## Production release

`productionPublicationPolicy.mastermind` admits the `tuturuuu-mastermind`
Worker for `mastermind.tuturuuu.com` only; `workers_dev` and preview URLs
stay off and the source declares no routes. A production sync that touches
the app (or the shared fleet contract) calls `mastermind-cloudflare.yaml` on
the `production` ref:

1. `artifact` builds once, seals the archive and runs the emitted-Worker
   acceptance for that exact commit.
2. `production-policy` evaluates the publication policy; deleting or
   holding the entry stops every later write.
3. `deploy` (GitHub environment `mastermind-production`, secret
   `MASTERMIND_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) restores and re-verifies the sealed
   archive, converts it to cf Build Output without rebuilding and requires the
   Worker secret names `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`, `CF_ACCESS_AUD`,
   `MASTERMIND_OWNER_EMAIL`, `OWNER_IDS` and `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`.
   Holding the deploy slot, it publishes only when the run's commit is still
   the `production` head, so a rerun of an older run publishes nothing. It
   captures the serving version, uploads the new one, records its id, checks
   the head again, and moves traffic only while the captured version still
   serves; a run overtaken during upload leaves its version without traffic. The first
   release creates the Worker, which answers 503 until its secrets exist.
4. With `MASTERMIND_HOST_ATTACHED=true` and `MASTERMIND_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`
   set, every probed path (`/`, the locales, `/login`, `/verify-token`, a
   server function, an asset, `/api/build-info`) must answer an anonymous
   request with a 302 to that team's Access login for this host. After any
   failure the captured version is assigned back only while this run's own
   version is serving. Receipts are kept for 30 days. A deployment marker is
   recorded only for an existing, configured Worker whose host check passed;
   the owner's signed-in acceptance on the live host stays a manual gate.

The planner calls the workflow (`deploy-mastermind-cloudflare`) when a
production sync changes its inputs, and looks up its marker like the other
Cloudflare targets. Until the first marker exists, release explicitly with
`gh workflow run mastermind-cloudflare.yaml --ref production`.

Traffic changes are serialized by the deploy concurrency group, and each
assignment re-reads the serving version first (`--expect-current`). Run a
manual assignment only while no release run is in progress, so an operator
change and a workflow rollback never race.

Manual rollback is one step:
`node scripts/ci/void-cf-publisher.mjs assign --worker tuturuuu-mastermind --version <previous version id>`
with the version from the run's `mastermind-release-*` receipt.

Provisioned outside the source, by name: the Access self-hosted application
for `mastermind.tuturuuu.com` (owner-only email policy, 24-hour session,
`HttpOnly` cookie; its AUD is `CF_ACCESS_AUD`), the Worker custom domain
`mastermind.tuturuuu.com` (DNS), the five Worker secrets, the
`mastermind-production` environment with `MASTERMIND_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`,
the variables `MASTERMIND_HOST_ATTACHED` and `MASTERMIND_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`
and, on the gateway,
`GATEWAY_MASTERMIND_REDIRECT`. The account's Access identity provider is
one-time PIN; a Google identity provider needs its own OAuth client.

A real-browser smoke that loads, refreshes and answers through the compiled
server functions, MFA and live permission acceptance, and the revocation
checks run on the live host before the gateway redirect is enabled.
Follow the [native Start runbook](/build/devops/native-start-migration).
